findings.rationale: The fixed bootstrap executor is not the only pre-R3 completion path. In run_dg10_serving_characterization.py, _stream_completion replays post-R3 authority, but _json_completion opens its supplied URL directly and _opencode_completion invokes docker/OpenCode directly without calling the post-R3 gate or requiring a validated capability. Both helpers are independently callable, so non-bootstrap model calls remain reachable before R3 acceptance.
findings.required_action: Require fixed post-R3 authorization or an unforgeable capability inside _json_completion and _opencode_completion before any opener or subprocess side effect. Add direct pre-R3 tests proving neither transport is invoked, while retaining the fixed 24-slot adapter as the sole pre-R3 path.
findings.title: Non-bootstrap completion helpers remain reachable without R3 acceptance

findings.rationale: _json_completion accepts an arbitrary URL and calls _NO_PROXY_OPENER.open without an authorization check. _opencode_completion calls openworker_e2e._run with docker exec and likewise has no local gate. The ordinary harness constructor is gated, but the helpers do not require an actual OpenWorkerHarness or its capability and can be called directly. The source-closure regression test only checks that a gate marker occurs somewhere in a file containing a completion literal, so the protected _stream_completion marker masks these unprotected transports.
findings.required_action: Place one non-bypassable candidate-bound authorization check immediately at every completion transport, including buffered HTTP and OpenCode subprocess execution. Add adversarial direct-helper tests with opener and subprocess spies, and replace the file-level marker scan with call-site-sensitive enforcement.
findings.title: Runnable buffered HTTP and OpenCode completion transports bypass authorization
